sentences.text: The CBTC supervision boundary at junctions is defined by the commanded route state, detected point position, and confirmed track vacancy rather than by geographic chainage alone.
East Junction Interlocking is also known locally as Falcon for maintenance callouts and legacy panel references.
North District Zone Controller requests routes through East Junction Interlocking only when the requested path is consistent with the current movement authority and the train approach profile.
South District Zone Controller applies the same route protection principles for interfaces with West Junction Interlocking, including checks on flank protection and conflicting movement locking.
The interlocking retains final vital authority for point movement, point locking, route locking, and release of protected sections.
CBTC supervision treats a route as available only after the relevant interlocking reports points detected, locked, and proved in the required position.
A requested route is not incorporated into a movement authority until the associated overlap and flank conditions are confirmed as protected.
If the interlocking reports loss of point correspondence after a route has been granted, the affected movement authority is shortened or withdrawn according to the safe braking envelope.
Axle counter clear and occupied indications are used as independent wayside evidence for route availability and for the continued integrity of route locking.
Where axle counter occupation conflicts with the train location estimated by the CBTC system, the more restrictive state is applied until the discrepancy is resolved.
East Junction Interlocking sends the Axle Counter Reset Request under the configured degraded-mode reset procedure.
Reset processing is inhibited while any associated route remains locked or while a train is approaching the affected detection section.
Maple verifies local track clearance evidence and records the result before authorising restoration of normal route setting after a detection anomaly.
West Junction Interlocking sends the Route Release Exception List when normal sectional release cannot be completed within the configured timing rules.
The zone controller treats any release exception as a retained hazard until the affected path is excluded from new movement authorities.
Platform approach protection is enforced by combining the active route state with train stopping accuracy supervision near the platform berth.
The Platform Screen Door Controller provides door closed and locked indications to the supervising wayside systems, but those indications do not replace interlocking route proof.
If platform door readiness is absent, the approaching train may be held outside the platform stopping window even when the junction route is otherwise proved.
The Atlas Onboard Controller uses the token bundle to validate that onboard operating context is current before accepting supervised route-related data.
Train Radio Modem messages carrying route status are exchanged through Wayside Radio Access Network paths with sequence monitoring and timeout handling.
Safety Data Communication Network paths between the zone controllers and the interlockings are configured for deterministic delivery of vital state changes and command acknowledgements.
Metro Operations Control System displays the commanded route, locked route, point state, and track occupancy state as separate indications so that control staff can identify mismatches.
A Line Traffic Controller may request a regulating action, but the request is executed only if the interlocking and CBTC protection rules agree that the route remains safe.
The Maintenance Diagnostic Server records route command outcomes, point operation timing, and detection transitions for later engineering review without participating in vital decisions.
